statement: A right circular cone is inscribed in a sphere of radius $R$ so that its base is parallel to a great circle. (i) If the cone has height $h$, show that its base radius $r$ satisfies $r^{2}=2Rh-h^{2}$. (ii) Find the height that maximises the volume and the maximum volume.
solution: (i) Cross-section: the sphere centre, the cone apex and a base point form a right triangle giving $r^{2}+(h-R)^{2}=R^{2}$, so $r^{2}=2Rh-h^{2}$. (ii) $V=\\frac{\\pi}{3}r^{2}h=\\frac{\\pi}{3}(2Rh^{2}-h^{3})$. $dV/dh=\\frac{\\pi}{3}(4Rh-3h^{2})=0$ gives $h=4R/3$ (and $h=0$). Then $V_{\\max}=\\frac{\\pi}{3}\\left(2R\\frac{16R^{2}}{9}-\\frac{64R^{3}}{27}\\right)=\\frac{32\\pi R^{3}}{81}$.
hints: Use the sphere's cross-section to relate $r$ and $h$.
